appraisal_events.evidence: Her «excès de froideur et d'insignifiance» is read as «une ruse destinée à dépister les soupçons»; the loud «Oui, j'irai vers cinq heures au tennis», the bicycle ridden off at speed, the flag alibi, and finally «je l'ai presque frôlée en passant, je l'ai bousculée», which two evenings later no longer means bad manners but a signal to a woman — «une parole de celle que nous aimons ne se conserve pas longtemps dans sa pureté ; elle se gâte, elle se pourrit».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator builds a case of concealed assignations against Albertine while explicitly diagnosing the rot that his own memory works on her words, so the passage stages the suspicion without ratifying it.

appraisal_events.evidence: With «un œil poché», he repeatedly mistakes the twin at «Aux Cerisiers» — «jouant sans le savoir Amphitryon», he asks the wrong tomato for a rendezvous and «recevait aussitôt une solide "tournée"», twice in one meal; reduced to warning strangers off tomatoes at the Grand-Hôtel, he is credited by Aimé with cunning — «C'est un vieux malin que Monsieur Bernard» — and keeps away from greeting anyone because of his eye.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narration turns him into pure farce: beaten, myopic, hiding his face, and misread even in his humiliation by the headwaiter who takes his disgust for a trick.

status_effects.explanation: Locally she is placed under a sustained imputation of duplicity — every coldness, errand and explanation read as cover — though the narration flags the reading as corrupted rather than proven.
He is the one who visibly suffers and depends: «je n'en fus que plus malheureux», his peace hostage to gestures he cannot interpret and to the reassurances she chooses to give him.
He is comprehensively ridiculed — black-eyed, beaten for mistaking one twin for the other, and finally comic even to the hotel staff.

ambiguities: Whether Albertine is in fact concealing anything is left open: the passage supplies only the narrator's readings and then undercuts them by describing how a beloved's words decay in memory, so her diminishment is a suspicion the text declines to confirm.
